#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <string>
#include <cstring>
using namespace std;

long long dp[2005][25][11]; // assume max length 2000, adjust dynamically if needed
// We'll allocate dynamically to be safe.

string s;
int n;

long long go(const string& A, int i, int pv, int v) {
    if (i == n) {
        return (pv == 0) ? 1 : 0;
    }
    if (dp[i][pv][v] != -1) return dp[i][pv][v];
    long long ans = 0;
    if (A[i] == '_') {
        for (int j = 0; j < 10; ++j) {
            if (i == 0 && j == 0) continue;
            int y = (pv * 10 + j) % 25;
            ans += go(A, i + 1, y, v);
        }
    } else if (A[i] == 'X') {
        if (v != 10) {
            ans += go(A, i + 1, (pv * 10 + v) % 25, v);
        } else {
            for (int j = 0; j < 10; ++j) {
                if (i == 0 && j == 0) continue;
                int y = (pv * 10 + j) % 25;
                ans += go(A, i + 1, y, j);
            }
        }
    } else {
        int d = A[i] - '0';
        ans += go(A, i + 1, (pv * 10 + d) % 25, v);
    }
    return dp[i][pv][v] = ans;
}

int main() {
    int t = 1; // Java had ttt=1 always
    while (t--) {
        cin >> s;
        n = s.length();
        // allocate dp dynamically
        // We'll use vector for safety, but to match Java static array we can use static size.
        // Since n is known, use vector.
        vector<vector<vector<long long>>> dp(n+1, vector<vector<long long>>(25, vector<long long>(11, -1)));
        // Use a reference to dp in go? We'll make go function use global dp or pass reference.
        // To keep code simple, we redefine go to use global dp. But dp is local. We'll pass reference.
        // Actually, we can make dp global with maximal size, but we don't know maximal size.
        // For simplicity, we allocate with max size 2000. If n>2000, we need dynamic.
        // Since Java code used static array with size A.length+1, we can dynamically allocate.
        // We'll rewrite go as lambda? Better to keep function signature and pass dp by reference.
        // To match Java exactly, we can use global DP but reallocate each test case.
        // We'll just allocate a local dp and pass to go via a wrapper or make go a lambda.
        // Easiest: redefine go to accept dp reference.
        // But the original Java code used static dp, so we can allocate a static size up to 2000, but input may be longer.
        // I'll assume max length 1000 to be safe, but the code should work for any length.
        // Alternatively, we can use a function that uses a global dp defined with max size from input.
        // Since we only have one test case, we can allocate after reading n.
        // So we'll create a lambda that captures dp by reference.
        auto go = [&](int i, int pv, int v) -> long long {
            if (i == n) return (pv == 0) ? 1 : 0;
            if (dp[i][pv][v] != -1) return dp[i][pv][v];
            long long ans = 0;
            if (s[i] == '_') {
                for (int j = 0; j < 10; ++j) {
                    if (i == 0 && j == 0) continue;
                    int y = (pv * 10 + j) % 25;
                    ans += go(i + 1, y, v);
                }
            } else if (s[i] == 'X') {
                if (v != 10) {
                    ans += go(i + 1, (pv * 10 + v) % 25, v);
                } else {
                    for (int j = 0; j < 10; ++j) {
                        if (i == 0 && j == 0) continue;
                        int y = (pv * 10 + j) % 25;
                        ans += go(i + 1, y, j);
                    }
                }
            } else {
                int d = s[i] - '0';
                ans += go(i + 1, (pv * 10 + d) % 25, v);
            }
            return dp[i][pv][v] = ans;
        };
        // handle edge cases as in Java
        if (n == 1 && s[0] == '0') {
            cout << "1\n";
            return 0;
        }
        if (s[0] == '0') {
            cout << "0\n";
            return 0;
        }
        if (n == 1) {
            if (s[0] == 'X' || s[0] == '_') {
                cout << "1\n";
                return 0;
            }
        }
        // fill dp with -1 was done by initialization
        cout << go(0, 0, 10) << "\n";
    }
    return 0;
}
